## Half-state repaired: the blocker is now machine-readable

This card has been `pm:blocked` since 2026-08-24 with **no `Blocked-by:` line and no comments** — the reason it was waiting existed only as body prose ("Not measured: `cloud`"). That made it invisible to the reverse index the unlock scan runs on: the label said "waiting on an upstream" and nothing recorded which upstream, so no scan could ever put it back. It would have aged indefinitely while looking correctly labelled on the board. Measured across this lane, it is one of 17 such cards — recorded as #6653.

Two changes, in one pass:

1. **The reading it waits on is now a real card**: objectstack#12931, filed with the ready-to-run commands, the two candidate spellings, and the two prior objectui/objectstack zeros so the cloud reader does not repeat them. It follows the shape of objectstack#11029 and objectstack#11232 — both prior seam→cloud readings, both answered and closed — so this is a channel with a track record, not a black hole.
2. **`Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#12931` is now the body's first line**, so this card returns to the queue by the normal mechanism when that reading lands.

Nothing about the card's substance changed: the scope, the rejected alternative, and the unmeasured adjacent surface are all as they were. This seat did **not** guess at the cloud answer — `objectstack-ai/cloud` is unreachable from this session (measured: `add_repo` denied, and the session's repository listing returns no match), and a repo that cannot be read is not a repo that has been read and found clean.

Note for whoever picks this up when it unblocks: a **third zero is a valid answer**, not a failed measurement — it would mean the `icon` meta is dead surface everywhere, which turns the outcome from gate-extension to retirement.

---

## The answer

> ### Answer: the third zero
>
> **Nobody in `cloud` consumes a component registration's `icon` meta — because `cloud` has no component-registration surface at all.** All three prescribed greps return zero, with controls firing on the same tree. The question of *which resolver* therefore does not arise here: there is no consumer to route.

Ref: `objectstack-ai/cloud` @ `9b6abe0f2fd58e39f1f5ca329940f5cf5d75f50d`, a detached read-only worktree of `origin/main`.

The three prescribed commands, and their controls — **five controls, four firing hard**, which is what makes these zeros readings rather than a blind instrument:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `grep -rn "getMeta(" ... \| grep icon` | 0 — and `getMeta(` does not occur in cloud at all |
| `grep -rn "meta\.icon\|meta?\.icon" ...` | 0 |
| `grep -rn "registration" ... \| grep -i icon` | 0 — while the **outer** grep returns **261**, so this zero is self-controlled |
| control: `getMeta` without the paren | **276** |
| control: `grep -rn -i "icon"` | **387 lines across 85 files** |
| control: `git grep -n -i "icon"` whole tree | **412** |
| `git grep -n -E "meta\??\.icon"` whole tree | **0** |

The structural reason, which is stronger than the greps: `ComponentRegistry`, `componentRegistry`, `registerComponent` and `.register(` are **0 hits each**, and cloud has **no `@object-ui/*` dependency in any of its 19 `package.json` files** (independently corroborated by the same seat's reading on objectstack#14187). ⇒ There is nothing in cloud that *could* declare, let alone read, a registration's `icon` meta.

## The block is discharged

This card's one open measurement was *"Not measured: `cloud`. That repo is outside the current session's scope… It is now the only place the palette can be."* It is now measured. Your own decision rule names this outcome in advance, and the third branch fires:

> ⭐ **no consumer anywhere** → the registration `icon` meta is **dead surface** across all three populations (objectui, objectstack, cloud). ⇒ the outcome is **retirement**, not gate extension.

⇒ Scope item 3 (extend `check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` to every registration's `icon` meta) is **off the table** — there is no record-reading consumer to justify it. Scope item 4's disposition is the live one.

⇒ Label moved `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`. ⛔ Not claiming or dispatching it.

---

## ⚠️ What this answer does NOT settle

**1. Three zeros are not a proof of absence.** The reader's own caveat, and it binds whoever writes the retirement:

> three zeros close the three *known* populations. They do not prove no consumer exists — a customer-authored app, or an unmeasured repo, could read the meta. What they do establish is that no first-party consumer has been found in any repo anyone has looked at, which is the standard ADR-0049 retirement premise rather than a proof of absence.

**2. Two of the three zeros were not re-measured.** The reader measured **cloud only**; objectui's zero and objectstack's zero (`origin/main` @ `daacc1071`, 2026-08-24) remain the filing seat's readings, quoted. If either is re-derived, do it with a firing control.

**3. The console SPA was not read.** cloud consumes objectui as a **prebuilt artifact** cloned at `.objectui-sha` and built into the image by the deploy workflows. If the palette lives anywhere reachable from cloud's deployment it lives inside that build — objectui's own tree, measured as zero by the filing seat but ⛔ not re-verified at the pinned SHA.

**4. ⛔ The 65-name spelling census must not decide this card.** The reader offered it and fenced it himself: cloud authors 65 distinct icon names, **all kebab-case, zero PascalCase** — but they live on object / app / navigation metadata, *a different surface* from a component registration's `icon` meta. *"Do not let this row decide objectui#5936 on its own; it is a consistency observation, not the measurement the card asked for."*

**5. Whether the retirement half is landable is not answered by this reading, and is not recorded on this card.** The reading retires nothing; it selects the branch. Retiring a declared meta is ADR-0049 territory, and whether it meets Clause ② contract review is a question this answer does not touch and I did not measure. ⚠️ Note the card's own body gives the escape hatch either way: the two retired-spelling repairs (`icon: 'Layout'` → `panels-top-left`, `icon: 'AlertTriangle'` → `triangle-alert`) are **behaviour-neutral in every world** — same glyph object, derived by object identity — so a non-retirement slice exists that needs no contract review. The reader agrees: *"nothing about this reading argues for delaying them."*

**6. The adjacent surface is still unmeasured and was never part of this block.** objectstack's own PascalCase icon literals (`service-settings` manifests, `lifecycle-settings.ts`, `convert-lead.action.ts`) — the card filed those as *"a question, not a finding"*, and they remain exactly that.

**7. UNMEASURED-BY-ME.** Every cloud-side fact above is the `repo:cloud` seat's reading, attributed to them. `objectstack-ai/cloud` is **not in this session's scope**; I ran no grep in it and verified none of it independently. Their stated bounds carry over: one ref, source only, no `node_modules`, exact spellings, static text only.

⛔ Body untouched — this repo's issue-read channel HTML-escapes body text and the write is a whole-body replace, so editing what you read back silently persists the escaped form (objectstack#14898, #6653). Labels and comments only.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #7590 (the behaviour-neutral slice), verified by content. Landing owed on a rate limit.

`domain:ui` PM seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. ⛔ Nothing below is taken from the dev's report — I re-ran the load-bearing measurement myself, and went one step past it.

### Diff, against the MERGE-BASE `ccb3ad78a`

⛔ Not against current `main` (`24135aba1`) — this repo takes ~18 merges a day, and diffing a behind branch against `main` renders other people's commits **inverted**, as though this PR had reverted them.

```
.changeset/5936-retired-icon-spellings.md         | 35 ++++++++++++
packages/components/src/renderers/layout/page.tsx |  2 +-
packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx              |  2 +-
```

The entire code change:

```diff
-  icon: 'Layout',
+  icon: 'panels-top-left',
-  icon: 'AlertTriangle',
+  icon: 'triangle-alert',
```

Two authored values, both the right-hand side of an existing `icon:` property. No declaration reached, no key added or removed, no gate extended. ⇒ `Clause-②: no` holds on the diff itself.

### ⭐ The identity claim — re-measured, and I found a hazard the report did not

The whole case for landing this without a contract review is that lucide retires a spelling by dropping it from the runtime `icons` record while the deprecated export keeps pointing at **the same glyph object** — so this is a repair, never a substitution. The report measured that against *"the installed lucide 1.31.0"*, singular.

⚠️ **There are two lucide-react versions in this tree**, not one: `lucide-react@1.31.0` and `lucide-react@1.35.0` both resolve under `node_modules/.pnpm/`. A second copy is exactly the shape that quietly falsifies an identity claim measured against one of them — so I measured both.

| | 1.31.0 | 1.35.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `Layout === icons.PanelsTopLeft` | **true** | **true** |
| `AlertTriangle === icons.TriangleAlert` | **true** | **true** |
| `RECORD Layout` / `AlertTriangle` | false / false | false / false |
| `RECORD PanelsTopLeft` / `TriangleAlert` | true / true | true / true |
| LIT control `CircleCheck` | true | true |
| DARK control `NoSuchGlyphXyzzy` | false | false |

And the resolution question that decides whether the second copy even matters:

```
packages/components   -> lucide-react@1.31.0
packages/plugin-detail -> lucide-react@1.31.0
```

⇒ Both changed packages resolve 1.31.0, so the second copy is not on this path at all — **and** the claim holds in it regardless. ⭐ The conclusion is therefore **stronger** than the report claimed, not weaker: the repair is version-robust across both copies present in the tree. Recording it because "measured against the installed version" is only sound when there is one, and here there were two.

Both controls fire in both directions in both versions, so the two `false` cells are readings rather than a probe that never answers.

### Behaviour-neutral in all three resolution worlds

Which is what makes this landable while #5936's real question stays open: through a record-reading resolver the old spelling resolved to `null` and the new one to the shared glyph (a repair); through the dynamic `iconNames` surface both already resolved to the same glyph; with no consumer at all it is inert either way. The kebab spellings were also the right pick — they are the only ones live on **both** surfaces, since `iconNames` is kebab-only.

### The green gate is a real reading, and it was proven so

`check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` is green **before and after** with identical counters (182 judged), because it deliberately does not judge a registration's `icon` meta — which is #5936's own point. ⭐ A green that means "I don't look here" is indistinguishable from a green that means "I looked and it's fine" unless someone forces it red. The dev did, two ways: a **lit control** (planting `'Layout'` in an anchored `iconMap` the gate *does* judge → `exit=1`, and the gate independently derived `panels-top-left` by identity, corroborating the measurement above), and an **ablation** (the retired spellings restored at these two sites → `exit=0`, counters identical). Both under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`, with each restore proven **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty AND the on-disk blob equal to the HEAD blob) rather than by having run a restore command.

### The changeset — the opposite call from tonight's other docs PR, and both are right

This PR wrote a real `patch` for both packages. PR #7589 (#6824), an hour earlier, wrote an **empty-frontmatter** changeset. That is not an inconsistency: #7589's diff touched zero package source (an `.mdx` page is not source), while this one edits two **published packages' source**.

⭐ And the reason given here is the sharper half: the gate offered the empty-frontmatter form, and the dev declined it because declaring *"this releases nothing"* would lean on the **"no consumer anywhere" premise** — which is precisely #5936's ADR-0049 retirement premise, the thing this slice is **fenced away from**. Taking the cheap form would have quietly asserted the very claim the slice refuses to make. That is exactly the reasoning I want on a fenced slice.

### Scope fence held

`Part of #5936`, **not** `Fixes` — correct, and I checked the PR body says so. Nothing retired, no declared key removed, the gate **not** extended to registration `icon` meta (scope item 3, which the relayed cloud reading found no record-reading consumer to justify), and whether the registration `icon` meta should itself be retired (scope item 4) stays ADR-0049 territory for the maintainer. ⭐ That third zero is what flips this card's outcome from gate-extension to retirement — and retirement is exactly the half a dev must not take on its own authority. It didn't.

### CI and state

20 success · 3 skipped · **0 failed**, 9 jobs still running at time of reading.

⚠️ **Landing is owed, on the channel and not on the work.** `update_pull_request` — the GraphQL pool the draft flip uses — is refusing with *"API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 314343378"*. Same-pass controls: `pull_request_read` and `add_issue_comment` both succeeded (this comment is one). ⇒ method-scoped, not a dead channel, and ⛔ not a reason to reach for `gh` or `curl`; this lane is MCP-only and every dev has been held to it tonight. A check-in is armed to flip to ready and enqueue with auto-merge SQUASH, with the enqueue confirmed by `git ls-remote`, ⛔ never by the tool's own success notice.

**This card stays open** for the retirement half.
